evidence: DeepSeek checks "p1[i] + p2[i] > T", "sum(p1) > T", and "sum(p2) > T"; GPT checks "check JOB condition" followed by "if sum1 > T" and "elif sum2 > T"; GLM uses the same three tests; Qwen derives "x_i <= T - p1 - p2".
affordance_in_statement: "JOB i" certifies that "x_i \ge 0", Separation, and Threshold cannot be simultaneously satisfied; "LOAD c" certifies orthogonality together with "x_i + p_{1,i} \le T" or "y_i + p_{2,i} \le T" for all i.
removal_suggestion: This is the intrinsic interval-packing structure: orthogonality forces the intervals to be disjoint, so feasibility is exactly a total-length capacity test. It cannot be removed by wording alone without changing the mathematical task; an effective edit would have to replace orthogonality or add a genuinely non-additive certificate condition.

common_affordance: The certificate subsystems collapse to one-dimensional interval-capacity inequalities: JOB is invalid exactly when p1_i+p2_i>T, while LOAD c is invalid exactly when the corresponding total length exceeds T.
recommended_edit: No semantics-preserving edit can defeat all survivors: this is the core mathematical structure of the task. To defeat the shortcut, change the subsystem definition so orthogonality is no longer equivalent to disjoint interval packing, for example by adding a non-additive interaction or weighting condition to LOAD certificates.
